reachable: Yes, at the scored kind of position and with real gradient. Verified by execution on the real training root with the genome's own stream, arch and batcher: the term fires on every batch (segmentation succeeds, 8.3-10.0% of the ~1900 command rows become anchors at batcher steps 1/500/3999), and a backward pass through `_prefix_route_term` alone puts non-zero gradient on exactly the 190 anchor rows of `pred` and nowhere else. The anchors are command-position predictions of read commands — the same object the scoring instrument reads at the withheld read — and their semantics are the intended ones: of 190 anchors, 106 pair with an earlier exposure whose content I traced through an explicit mv chain to the anchor's read path, 61 through a `cat X > Y` redirection copy, and only 21 are same-path zero-move re-reads. Anchor roles are cvar_test 104 / cups_test 64 / read 17. The three structural preconditions the term needs all hold on real data: (a) segmentation recovers the true sequence ids EXACTLY on every batch tested (64/64 segments, elementwise equal, including the batcher's duplicated sequences at late steps); (b) identical observation text yields bit-identical standardized target vectors — in-segment text-equality and embedding-equality agree on all 1901x1901 pairs, 0 mismatches; (c) with a non-identity target the term switches itself off as claimed (delta_prev target → 1837 singleton segments of 1901 rows → no anchors), and the genome pins target=identity anyway. Cost is not a threat: candidate loss 91.3 ms vs parent 89.8 ms on a 1901-row CPU batch (+2%); full fwd+bwd 1836 ms vs 1800 ms.
solves_outside_model: Clean. The objective parses no commands and touches no tokens: `_prefix_route_term` consumes only `pred`, the detached precision-weighted `tgt`, and `ctx["prev"]`, and `prev` is used solely to cut the flat rows into trajectories. Nothing resolved reaches the model's input — the mining is loss shaping over training rows whose answer observation is legitimately present. `loss()` is called only inside `evolve/harness.py::_train`; there is no call to any objective in `evolve/cups_ca.py` or `evolve/cups_probe.py`, so the term cannot run at the scored position and there is no mechanism that switches off there. The only command parsing anywhere in this genome is the parent's stream `r4_pathslot_dualaddress_code`, which is inherited unchanged and is covered by the read-token-parity gate. I verified by execution that `candidate_loss == parent_loss + 2.0 * prefix_term` to bit equality (delta 0.0) on a real batch, and by diff that the parent's body is preserved line-for-line — only NAME, DESCRIPTION and the final `return` were changed.
summary: The code does what its detailed specification says, and the specification is unusually well grounded — every mechanical assumption I could test on the real training root held. Segmentation from the strict-causal `prev` recovers the true sequence boundaries exactly (not approximately) on every batch I tried, including the real batcher's duplicate-heavy late batches; bit-identical observation text really does produce bit-identical standardized targets, so exact-equality classes are content identities with zero false pairs in 1901x1901 comparisons; the anchor mining picks out genuine routed re-reads (169 of 190 anchors trace through an explicit mv chain or a redirection copy from their paired earlier exposure); the parent objective is preserved to bit equality and the total is exactly parent + 2.0*prefix; gradient lands on exactly the anchor rows; and the cost is +2%. The author's stated MEASURED numbers are essentially right despite having no torch and no embeddings in the jail: claimed anchors 8-11% (measured 8.3-10.0%), mean candidate set 11.6 (measured 12.3), depths 1..12 (measured 1..14), 100x tighter equality threshold than the parent (1e-5 vs the parent's _EQ_FRAC 1e-3 — correct). Strictly, the check they describe ("rebuilding a 6-sequence batch ... and running the rule recovers the true sequence ids exactly") could only have been run on text as a proxy for embeddings, and the load-bearing assumption behind that proxy is exactly the one they could not test; I tested it and it is true. What does not survive is a piece of the RATIONALE, not the code. The claim that the prefix set "structurally guarantees" the location-keyed decoy is among the negatives is false: only 29% of anchors have any earlier read of the same location in their prefix, and the described A/B contrast occurs in 17%. And the ported mining rule silently drops the source head's different-command clause (`~dup_c`), so 12% of anchors (11.7% of the depth-weighted mass) are same-command re-reads on which a purely name-keyed predictor is correct and gets no gradient — contradicting "nothing in the term rewards any function of the read location alone". Neither can inflate comp_ca (a name-keyed predictor cancels structurally), so the failure mode is a weaker mechanism than advertised, not a shortcut. Two smaller labelling issues: "route depth" is really "mutating steps in the interval" (measured mean 3.77 vs 1.45 actual moves, r=0.77), and the class-size gap is narrower than described (classes of 5-7 exist; 26 read rows are misfiled as mutating). What I could not check: the actual effect on comp_ca, whether _LAMBDA_PREFIX=2.0 (28% of the loss at init) degrades the general fit enough to drop native_hit — the author names this as the main risk himself — and wall-clock on the GPU lane at the full 4000-step budget.
